evidence: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:246 uses `var`, which is function-scoped in ES5 and hoisted no matter where it sits, so a block would change nothing. The 'no case declarations' concern only applies to let/const. The same `var` in this case existed before the PR, which only changed the value it is set to.

Ruby does not cache Tempfile#size. It flushes and stats the open file descriptor (File#size uses fstat), or runs File.size on the path when the file is closed. ImageMagick `convert` in downsize_instructions (app/models/optimized_image.rb:126-135) opens the output path for writing and truncates the same inode, so fstat sees the new size. The stated mechanism is wrong. Small caveat: if ImageOptim.optimize_image! (optimized_image.rb:164) swaps the file by rename, the descriptor would point at the old inode, but that is not what the reviewer claims.

The codebase already downsizes and resizes in place with from == to: app/models/upload.rb:98 (OptimizedImage.resize(file.path, file.path, ...)) and app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14. ImageMagick reads the whole input before opening the output. The file is a per-request upload tempfile (uploads_controller.rb:58), not the user's only copy, so a failure fails this upload and loses nothing permanent.

The loop at app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:65-69 always ends: `attempt` starts at 5 and drops by 1 each pass, and the condition checks `attempt > 0`. At most 5 passes can run. The size is also not stale (see issue 1).

The size passed at uploads_controller.rb:72 comes from Tempfile#size, which stats the file on every call, so after an in-place convert it gives the downsized size. Switching to File.size(tempfile.path) does no harm but fixes no demonstrated bug; the 'cached size' premise is wrong.

app/models/optimized_image.rb:145 defines self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}), and line 149 defines self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={}) again. Ruby has no overloading, so the second definition replaces the first, and Ruby prints a 'method redefined' warning. Fix: keep one signature, or give the percentage version a different name or signature.

app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14 calls OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts) with 5 arguments. Only the definition at optimized_image.rb:149 survives, and it takes 3-4 arguments, so this raises ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments, given 5, expected 3..4). Emoji resizing breaks.

utilities.js:182 used to read Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'] (so the attachment and image limits were separate) and now uses a hardcoded 10 * 1024. The 413 message at utilities.js:246 and the API download limit at uploads_controller.rb:55 (10.megabytes) are hardcoded too. As a result max_attachment_size_kb is no longer checked in the browser, and sites whose limit is set above 10MB can't upload bigger files. Server-side downsizing (uploads_controller.rb:64) only applies to images, so non-image attachments don't benefit from the higher limit.

It is true that the inline `rescue nil` at uploads_controller.rb:55 swallows every exception. But it existed before this PR, which only changed the size argument from SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes to 10.megabytes. If the download fails, tempfile is nil, the downsize block is skipped (line 64), and create_for then fails. That is outside this PR's scope; adding logging would be a small optional improvement.
